Fuel from the cucumber peel you throw away

A Petroleum Engineering final-year project that ferments cucumber skin into bio-ethanol, distils it at four temperatures, and tests each batch by HPLC to find the cleanest one.

Why waste peel?

Oil demand keeps rising while fossil fuels add CO2 that stays in the air for centuries. Bio-ethanol can be blended into petrol and diesel to cut emissions. The question here: can a household waste product make it?

1st generation

Made from food crops like corn and sugarcane. Simple, but competes with food, land and water.

2nd generation: this project

Made from non-food biomass and waste. Cucumber is grown worldwide, and only the skin is used. No earlier work on cucumber skin was found in the literature review.

3rd generation

Made from algae. Fast growing, but yields are low and large volumes of culture are needed.

What the results show

  • Higher temperature collected 100 ml faster: 6 h at 75 °C down to 3.5 h at 90 °C.
  • Speed came at a cost. HPLC traces showed fewer impurity peaks at 85 °C than at 75, 80 or 90 °C.
  • The 90 °C sample looked better than 75 and 80 °C, but its baseline amplitude was higher than at 85 °C.
Conclusion. Of the four runs, bio-ethanol distilled at 85 °C showed the strongest alcohol presence by HPLC, so it is the best compromise between speed and cleanliness.

Where it goes next

  • Purify the extracted bio-ethanol further.
  • Measure the efficiency of the purified product.
  • Compare against ethanol made from other feedstocks.
  • Compare against commercial ethanol.

Abstract, certificate and declaration

Abstract. Population growth and industrialisation keep raising energy demand, and crude oil output is predicted to fall sharply by 2050. This work extracts bio-fuel from the skin of Cucumis sativus, a second-generation, eco-friendly source. The expected result was a fuel with properties similar to conventional ethanol and purity above 95%. Keywords: cucumber skin, alpha-amylase, renewable energy, bio-fuel, distillation.

Certificate. The report is certified as bonafide work of the four students for the B.Tech in Petroleum Engineering, 2023-24, signed by Dr. Sourav Mukherjee (Project Guide), Dr. Suman Paul (HOD), Dr. Shrishail Anadinni (Associate Dean) and Dr. Abdul Sharief (Dean).

Declaration. The team declares the work independent and not submitted elsewhere. Bengaluru, 16 January 2024.
